Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: weeks in a sprint, points a person finishes in a focused day, days after which a card or blocker is too old, healthy bug share, capacity limits.

Fill Projects with the projects that run sprints: manager, client, sponsor, client contact and vendor with their phones. Open points, ready points, velocity, the forecast date and the board counts fill in by themselves.
Fill Team with each person and Epics with the big pieces of work of each project. Then add every item to Product Backlog with its epic, type, priority, story points and status.

Create each sprint on Sprints with its dates, goal and committed points. Record the days and focus of every person on Sprint Capacity to see the capacity in points and a check against what is assigned.
During the sprint put the cards on Board Cards, set the limits on Work in Progress Limits and write each stand-up on Daily Stand-ups. Blocked cards and old cards show in red and amber.
Count the points remaining each day on Burndown Data and read the line against the ideal. The sprint shown on the chart is the one typed in the setting on Start.
When a card is finished add it to Cycle Times to see the cycle time and the cards finished each week. Record every blocker on Blockers with its cause, owner and dates.
After each sprint fill Sprint Reviews with the points accepted, Velocity by Sprint with a note, Retrospectives with the mood and Retrospective Actions with an owner and a due date for each action.

Use Backlog Refinement for your refinement sessions, Release Plan for each release and Acceptance Criteria so that done means the same for everyone. Working Agreements keeps your team rules and shows when to review them.

Use the 13 calculators for capacity, velocity, sprints left, the burndown check, the release date, points to days, work-in-progress limits, cycle time, the commitment, backlog health, bugs, epics and a what-if.
Print 10 sheets and 9 reports, follow 9 checklists and tap a message link to open a chat with the text and the number ready.
Read Sprints and Boards Dashboard and Charts every week: velocity, completion, blocked cards, cycle time, bug share, open retrospective actions and the sprints left.

Stakeholder map with quadrant and strategy
influence, interest and attitude place every stakeholder in a quadrant, give the strategy to follow and the days between contacts, and flag who is overdue
the level now and the level wanted show how many steps each stakeholder must move, with the action, its owner and its due date
attendees, length and the average cost per hour give the cost of every meeting, and each set of minutes is checked against your days allowed to send them
Action items with owner, due date and days overdue
every action from every meeting has an owner, a due date, days overdue and days to close, so nothing agreed in a meeting is lost
Weekly status report with a weighted score
four ratings give a weighted score, an honesty check against the overall rating, the weeks in red in a row and an escalation flag
green, amber and red counts, average progress and the change in red projects, from the weekly reports, in one row per week
every decision you need from a sponsor shows days waiting, days past the date needed and whether it was answered in time
Steering pack items with a project snapshot
each item shows the headline, the decision needed and the outcome next to the health, weeks in red, open actions and decisions waiting of its project
each update shows days to a reply and a reply check, and each client answer from 0 to 10 shows its band and whether a low score was followed up
audience, channel and frequency give the next send date, and every report you issue gets a due date moved to a working day
open, overdue and done actions, closure rate, average days to close, the next action due and the attendance rate for each person
the next four weeks of meetings show days to go, whether the agenda is ready or overdue, the expected cost and the project health behind them

Projects: sponsor, health, reports, actions and decisions
One row per project with client, manager, sponsor and dates; the latest health, weeks in red, report state, open and overdue actions, waiting decisions and next meeting fill in by themselves.
Team: who chairs meetings, owes reports and sends minutes
One row per team member with role, cost per hour and contact; meetings chaired, projects led, late reports, late minutes and contacts held fill in by themselves.
Stakeholder register with quadrant and strategy
One row per stakeholder with influence and interest from 1 to 5 and attitude; the quadrant, strategy, contact cadence, last contact, engagement gap and manager fill in by themselves.
Stakeholder map: quadrant by attitude and contact rhythm
One row per quadrant and attitude with the days between contacts you want; how many stakeholders sit in it, how many are overdue for contact and below the engagement wanted fill in by themselves.
Engagement plan: level now, level wanted and the action
One row per engagement action with the level now and the level wanted; the gap, check, quadrant, due state and phones fill in by themselves.
Communication plan: who hears what, how often, from whom
One row per message you send on a rhythm with audience, channel and frequency; the days between sends, the next date, the check and the owner phone fill in by themselves.
Report calendar: each report, audience and next due date
One row per report you issue with audience and frequency; the next due date moves to a working day, with days to due and a check, and fills in by itself from the last issue date.
Meetings: length, attendees, cost and minutes check
One row per meeting with type, date, chair, attendees and length; the month, person-hours, cost, actions raised and open, and whether the minutes went out in time fill in by themselves.
Meeting minutes: key points, decisions and when sent
One row per set of minutes with key points, decisions and the sent date; the meeting details, days to send, check, open actions and the client contact fill in by themselves.
Attendance: who was invited, who came and who sent apologies
One row per person and meeting (a meeting ID from Meetings or Upcoming Meetings) with present, apologies or absent; the title, date, project, phone and the apology deadline fill in by themselves.
Action items: owner, due date and days overdue
One row per action with owner, due date and status; the project, days overdue, days to close, state, owner and chair phones and the client contact fill in by themselves.
Weekly status reports: ratings, score and red run
One row per project and week with the four ratings, overall health and progress; the due date, state, weighted score, honesty check, weeks in red in a row and escalation flag fill in by themselves.

Client feedback: score from 0 to 10, comment and follow-up

Stakeholder contacts: every talk, outcome and next step

Upcoming meetings: next four weeks and agenda check
One row per planned meeting in the next four weeks with chair, length and agenda ready; days to go, agenda check, cost, project health, open actions and phones fill in by themselves.
Sponsor decisions: what you need and how long it waits
One row per decision you need from a sponsor with the date needed; days waiting, days to answer, whether it is late, the sponsor phone and the manager fill in by themselves.
Action owners: open, overdue and done per person
One row per team member; open, overdue and done actions, closure rate, share overdue, average days to close, the next due action and attendance rate fill in by themselves from the other sheets.
Portfolio by week: projects green, amber and red
One row per week (type the Monday); reports, green, amber and red counts, average progress, on time and late reports and the change against last week fill in by themselves from Weekly Status Reports.
